headline: Greenwood Leflore Hospital warns of closure as Medicaid moves to withhold $2.4 million payment
summary: The Mississippi Division of Medicaid is withholding a payment from Greenwood Leflore Hospital due to outstanding debts, potentially leading to its closure and disrupting healthcare services for residents. The hospital argues that this could harm public health by eliminating access to care. A plan to transfer operations to University of Mississippi Medical Center (UMMC) is underway, which aims to maintain services but faces legal challenges from the Division of Medicaid over debt repayment.

headline: Regents vote to increase NU tuition by 4.25%, cut $8 million in next $1.19 billion budget
summary: The University of Nebraska Board of Regents voted to increase tuition rates by about 4.25% across all campuses due to an $8 million budget cut, despite receiving a state funding increase of only 0.62%. The hike was justified as necessary to mitigate future cuts and give non-unionized faculty pay increases, but regents expressed concern about affordability for students. State funding slowdowns were lamented by NU leaders, with one regent encouraging Nebraskans to advocate for increased resources.

headline: 2 more cruise ship passengers leave Omaha quarantine after deadly hantavirus outbreak
summary: The University of Nebraska Medical Center's National Quarantine Unit cared for cruise ship passengers exposed to hantavirus. After five weeks, two more individuals left but were encouraged to monitor symptoms until June 21 due to potential late-onset symptoms. Public health departments coordinated their return and will oversee continued monitoring at home.

headline: Labor and faith groups decry federal indictment of 15 anti-ICE protesters
summary: Tens of thousands protested ICE agents' presence in Minnesota. Fifteen protesters face charges for actions against federal agents during Operation Metro Surge. Human Rights Watch reports human rights abuses during the operation.

headline: Minnesotans push back against the surveillance state
summary: A Minnesota woman's expedited airport security screening privileges were revoked after observing ICE operations, raising concerns about potential retaliation and surveillance of lawful protesters.

headline: New Mexico Secretary of State Maggie Toulouse Oliver suspends Dem Lt. Gov. campaign, citing health
summary: Maggie Toulouse Oliver, New Mexico's Secretary of State and Democratic nominee for Lieutenant Governor, suspended her campaign due to health concerns. The Democratic Party will select a replacement via its State Central Committee process.

headline: Despite $2.6B investment, NM schools ‘largely failed’ to increase instructional time, report says
summary: The Legislative Finance Committee report found that despite $2.6 billion invested since 2018 to increase instructional time, New Mexico schools have largely failed to achieve this goal due to chronic absenteeism and teacher absences. The Public Education Department Secretary called for more effective use of instructional time, while lawmakers expressed concern over lack of progress and potential one-size-fits-all policy decisions.

headline: Pride and Pain: Father’s Day in ICE detention in New Mexico
summary: At Torrance County Detention Facility in New Mexico, majority of ICE detainees are non-criminal men who struggle with separation from work and family due to detention. Many are prime-aged workers supporting families abroad. Detention disrupts their roles as fathers and breadwinners, impacting thousands of children daily.

headline: Polling shows Midwestern voters concerned about home insurance cost
summary: Midwestern homeowners surveyed express concern about rising insurance premiums, with 86% wanting officials to act more on reducing costs. They support policies holding utilities and polluters accountable, and want insurers to disclose factors affecting premiums. A majority feels federal, state, and local officials are doing too little to address the issue.

headline: Los republicanos de Kansas podrían intentar retrasar la elección al Senado si Marshall deja el cargo
summary: Una ley republicana en Kansas podría limitar el poder de la gobernadora demócrata Laura Kelly para cubrir vacantes en ciertos cargos electivos estatales, incluyendo el Senado de EE.UU. Esto ha generado especulaciones sobre si los republicanos intentarán evitar las elecciones para el Senado este año haciendo que el titular, Roger Marshall, renuncie para unirse a la administración de Donald Trump. Si Marshall renunciara, Kelly y la Legislatura serían responsables de implementar la ley de 2025, lo que podría debilitar el control del Partido Republicano en el Senado si un demócrata ocupara su escaño. Esta situación podría generar tensiones políticas y posibles desafíos legales.

headline: State workers fight Newsom’s return-to-office mandate
summary: State workers protesting Newsom's office return mandate; bill seeks more telework flexibility.

headline: Immigration raids have made skin color top of mind for a new generation of California Latinos
summary: The author recounts her father's experience of racial profiling by police decades ago, noting similarities to current immigration enforcement practices that target Latinos. Justice Kavanaugh's opinion in Noem v. Vasquez Perdomo suggests racial profiling can be valid for immigration policing. The article calls on Chicano communities to unite and challenge societal demonization of their men, highlighting past collective efforts like the Chicano Blowouts and Moratorium as examples of successful resistance.

headline: In the Shawnee: Alpha-gal syndrome poses threat to southern Illinoisans as tick population surges
summary: The Illinois Department of Public Health issued an alert after a spike in Legionnaires' disease cases in Chicago. The state is collaborating with local health departments and facilities to investigate and control the outbreak, which has affected over 120 people since August.

headline: ‘No one can credibly investigate themselves’: Now-cleared ‘Broadview Six’ protesters request special prosecutor
summary: No protests or civil unrest mentioned.

headline: Pressure front over West Virginia schools
summary: West Virginia allocates about 44% of its general budget to primary and secondary education but faces funding inequities due to a flawed school funding formula. This results in resource-rich areas like Berkeley County receiving substantial funds for growth, while struggling counties like Clay suffer from declining enrollment and inadequate resources, leading to school consolidations. Political power disparities exacerbate these issues as growing regions gain attention while declining ones are overlooked.

headline: Morrisey appoints new WV state budget director as long-time employees leave office
summary: Gov. Patrick Morrisey appointed Aaron Snodgrass as West Virginia's new state budget director following retirements of previous directors Mike McKown and Mark Muchow. Snodgrass brings extensive financial management experience, having previously served at the Department of Health Facilities where he oversaw a controversial $140 million divestiture involving long-term care facilities. The sale resulted in a loss of federal funding for remaining state-run facilities, potentially impacting future budget forecasts.

headline: Lamont wants to charge companies with employees on Medicaid
summary: Governor Ned Lamont proposes a $100 million annual revenue increase through a fee on large companies whose employees rely on Medicaid. This move aims to offset federal cuts and stabilize health premiums, potentially benefiting middle-class residents relying on Covered Connecticut for insurance. The proposal requires legislative approval if Lamont is reelected in January.

headline: CT special education advocates slam Trump Ed Dept. moves: an ‘assassination attempt’
summary: The Trump administration's decision to relocate two key special education offices has sparked concerns among Connecticut advocates who fear weakened federal oversight could lead to protests or civil unrest from affected communities.

headline: Immigration Authorities Kept an 8-Year-Old US Citizen in a Brooklyn Shelter for Nearly Seven Months
summary: A concerned advocate describes a detained immigrant minor as withdrawn and reluctant, highlighting potential mental health concerns amidst ongoing detention policies.

headline: Ohio Democrats urge Gov. DeWine to veto submetering bill
summary: Ohio Democrats urge Gov. Mike DeWine to veto House Bill 173, which sets rules for submetering companies serving apartments/condos but falls short of treating them as public utilities, as Ohio Supreme Court recently ruled. Democrats argue this bill risks rolling back consumer protections and could lead to protests from affected tenants if not revised or vetoed.

headline: No signs of emerging New World screwworm threat in WA
summary: A parasitic fly, the New World screwworm, has reinvaded the U.S. after a nearly 50-year absence, posing a threat to livestock and pets. Washington state has implemented new inspection requirements for livestock entering the state to prevent its spread. The USDA has allocated $105 million to control and eradicate the pest, which can cause painful wounds in both animals and humans but poses a low risk to people in the U.S., according to the CDC.

headline: West Texas organization sues Trump administration to stop border wall in Big Bend
summary: In Redford, Texas on June 5, 2026, protesters used a canoe as a symbolic sign against the construction of a border wall, demonstrating opposition to immigration policies.

headline: Alaska districts close 12 schools this year, amid severe budget cuts
summary: Alaska's education funding faces chronic shortfall, leading to school closures and staff cuts across districts. Lawmakers approved a $144M one-time increase but emphasized election reform over sustained education funding boosts.

headline: ICE empties ‘Alligator Alcatraz’ amid hurricane season. Activists aren’t buying it.
summary: ICE evacuated "Alligator Alcatraz," a remote Florida detention center, citing hurricane safety concerns. Environmental groups dispute this explanation, alleging it's a tactic to avoid environmental regulations while transferring detainees. The facility remains operational despite ICE's announcement, with supplies and buses still present. The evacuation doesn't seem to be permanent, as neither ICE nor Governor DeSantis' office confirmed its duration.

headline: UPDATE:  Police arrest suspect in deadly Wilmington Hospital shooting
summary: On June 16, a shooting incident at Wilmington Hospital left one ChristianaCare employee dead and another critically injured. The suspect, John Wallace-Bey, was arrested later that day in Philadelphia. The shooting prompted a lockdown of the hospital campus before resuming normal operations the next day.

headline: Congressman urges Gov. Bill Lee to revoke directive to report immigration status of sick kids
summary: Tennessee Rep. Steve Cohen urged Gov. Bill Lee to rescind a directive requiring immigration checks for around 400 children with critical health issues enrolled in Children’s Special Services program. Cohen argued that the policy targets vulnerable sick children and their families for deportation, calling it "morally repulsive." The state's Department of Health sent notices to parents warning of reporting requirements after June 30, raising concerns among healthcare providers and advocates who fear disruption of life-sustaining medical treatments.

headline: Community rallies behind Cleary University student detained by ICE as family seeks bond hearing
summary: Cleary University student Karliana Perdomo-Gotopo, a Venezuelan national and soccer team member, was detained by ICE at North Lake Processing Center. Her family and university community are working for her release on bond while facing challenges due to reduced bond hearings and low bond approval rates. Detention conditions at the facility have been criticized by immigrants' rights groups.
